opening.text: A seed in winter looks dead. It lies in cold ground, and nothing seems to happen. Then spring comes, and green shoots rise.
Death can feel like winter. Today I want to talk about what comes after, and why we can have hope.

mainMessage.text: Death is not the end. Our spirits live on. Jesus Christ broke the bonds of death, and everyone will be resurrected. Those who love Him will find peace and a place prepared. That hope can comfort us now.

blocks.text: Life continues.
Job knew that his Redeemer lives, and that he would see God in his flesh. Jesus told a dying man beside Him that he would be in paradise that very day.
For I know that my redeemer liveth, and that he shall stand at the latter day upon the earth: And though after my skin worms destroy this body, yet in my flesh shall I see God:
And Jesus said unto him, Verily I say unto thee, To day shalt thou be with me in paradise.
President Thomas S. Monson of the First Presidency wrote this in his article “‘He Is Risen’: A Prophet’s Testimony” in the April 2012 Ensign. It is a magazine article, not a conference talk.
The darkness of death can ever be dispelled by the light of revealed truth.
Death is a doorway, not a wall.
Jesus Christ opened the way.
Paul taught that Christ was the first to rise. In Adam all die, and in Christ all will live. Jesus Himself said, “I am the resurrection, and the life.”

But now is Christ risen from the dead, and become the firstfruits of them that slept. For since by man came death, by man came also the resurrection of the dead. For as in Adam all die, even so in Christ shall all be made alive.

Jesus said unto her, I am the resurrection, and the life: he that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live: And whosoever liveth and believeth in me shall never die. Believest thou this?
President Thomas S. Monson of the First Presidency wrote this in his article “‘He Is Risen’: A Prophet’s Testimony” in the April 2012 Ensign. It is a magazine article, not a conference talk.
I declare my personal witness that death has been conquered, victory over the tomb has been won.
Because He lives, we will live.
The spirit goes home.
Alma was taught that our spirits return to God. The righteous enter paradise, a state of rest and peace. President Joseph F. Smith saw a great company of faithful spirits gathered together.

Now, concerning the state of the soul between death and the resurrection—Behold, it has been made known unto me by an angel, that the spirits of all men, as soon as they are departed from this mortal body, yea, the spirits of all men, whether they be good or evil, are taken home to that God who gave them life. And then shall it come to pass, that the spirits of those who are righteous are received into a state of happiness, which is called paradise, a state of rest, a state of peace, where they shall rest from all their troubles and from all care, and sorrow.

As I pondered over these things which are written, the eyes of my understanding were opened, and the Spirit of the Lord rested upon me, and I saw the hosts of the dead, both small and great. And there were gathered together in one place an innumerable company of the spirits of the just, who had been faithful in the testimony of Jesus while they lived in mortality;
President Thomas S. Monson of the First Presidency said this in his talk “I Know That My Redeemer Lives” from the April 2007 general conference.
Though difficult and painful, death is an essential part of our mortal experience.
It is a place of peace, and our loved ones are not alone.
Every body will rise.
Alma taught that spirit and body will be joined again. Nothing will be lost, and all will be made whole. Nephi taught that a power of resurrection had to come.

The soul shall be restored to the body, and the body to the soul; yea, and every limb and joint shall be restored to its body; yea, even a hair of the head shall not be lost; but all things shall be restored to their proper and perfect frame.

For as death hath passed upon all men, to fulfil the merciful plan of the great Creator, there must needs be a power of resurrection, and the resurrection must needs come unto man by reason of the fall; and the fall came by reason of transgression; and because man became fallen they were cut off from the presence of the Lord.
Elder Dallin H. Oaks of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Resurrection” from the April 2000 general conference.
Because of the resurrection, we know that these mortal deficiencies are only temporary!
What was weak will be made whole.
A place is prepared.
Jesus told His friends He was going ahead to prepare a place for them. Peter wrote that He also taught the spirits who had not yet heard the gospel, so no one is forgotten.

In my Father’s house are many mansions: if it were not so, I would have told you. I go to prepare a place for you. And if I go and prepare a place for you, I will come again, and receive you unto myself; that where I am, there ye may be also.

For Christ also hath once suffered for sins, the just for the unjust, that he might bring us to God, being put to death in the flesh, but quickened by the Spirit: By which also he went and preached unto the spirits in prison;
President Thomas S. Monson of the First Presidency said this in his talk “I Know That My Redeemer Lives” from the April 2007 general conference.
Because our Savior died at Calvary, death has no hold upon any one of us.
No one is left out.
Comfort for those who mourn.
The Lord said it is right to weep for those who die. He also said that those who die in Him will find it sweet. John saw a day when God will wipe away all tears.

Thou shalt live together in love, insomuch that thou shalt weep for the loss of them that die, and more especially for those that have not hope of a glorious resurrection. And it shall come to pass that those that die in me shall not taste of death, for it shall be sweet unto them;
And God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes; and there shall be no more death, neither sorrow, nor crying, neither shall there be any more pain: for the former things are passed away.
Elder Dallin H. Oaks of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Resurrection” from the April 2000 general conference.
The assurance of immortality also helps us bear the mortal separations involved in the death of our loved ones.
Grief and hope can live in the same heart.

story.title: Lazarus, come forth

blocks.text: Lazarus had been in the tomb for four days when Jesus Christ came.

And when he thus had spoken, he cried with a loud voice, Lazarus, come forth. And he that was dead came forth, bound hand and foot with graveclothes: and his face was bound about with a napkin. Jesus saith unto them, Loose him, and let him go.
Jesus Christ called Lazarus by name, and he came out. The voice that raised one man will one day call everyone. Death does not have the last word.

story.title: He is not here, but is risen

blocks.text: Some women went to the tomb early in the morning to care for the body of Jesus Christ. Two angels spoke to them.

And as they were afraid, and bowed down their faces to the earth, they said unto them, Why seek ye the living among the dead? He is not here, but is risen: remember how he spake unto you when he was yet in Galilee,
The tomb was empty. The women went in sorrow, and they left with news that changed the world. The empty tomb is why we can look at our own loss with hope.

story.title: I see the heavens opened

blocks.text: Stephen was about to die for his faith. Just before, he looked up.

But he, being full of the Holy Ghost, looked up steadfastly into heaven, and saw the glory of God, and Jesus standing on the right hand of God, And said, Behold, I see the heavens opened, and the Son of man standing on the right hand of God.
Stephen’s last moments were full of light, not fear. He saw Jesus Christ waiting for him. We can trust that the Savior will be there for us too.

story.title: Damsel, arise

blocks.text: A man named Jairus asked Jesus Christ to help his young daughter, who had died. Jesus went to her.

And he took the damsel by the hand, and said unto her, Talitha cumi; which is, being interpreted, Damsel, I say unto thee, arise. And straightway the damsel arose, and walked; for she was of the age of twelve years. And they were astonished with a great astonishment.
He took her gently by the hand, as a parent wakes a child in the morning. One day He will do the same for each of us.

Death is not the last stop. Job knew he would see God. Jesus told a dying man he would be with Him in paradise that day.
For I know that my redeemer liveth, and that he shall stand at the latter day upon the earth: And though after my skin worms destroy this body, yet in my flesh shall I see God:
And Jesus said unto him, Verily I say unto thee, To day shalt thou be with me in paradise.
President Thomas S. Monson of the First Presidency wrote this in his article “‘He Is Risen’: A Prophet’s Testimony” in the April 2012 Ensign. It is a magazine article, not a conference talk.
The darkness of death can ever be dispelled by the light of revealed truth.
The road does not end in the dark.
The way was paved.
A trip is easier on a paved road. Jesus Christ paved this one. Paul said He rose first and that all will follow. Jesus said that whoever believes in Him will live.

But now is Christ risen from the dead, and become the firstfruits of them that slept. For since by man came death, by man came also the resurrection of the dead. For as in Adam all die, even so in Christ shall all be made alive.

Jesus said unto her, I am the resurrection, and the life: he that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live: And whosoever liveth and believeth in me shall never die. Believest thou this?
President Thomas S. Monson of the First Presidency wrote this in his article “‘He Is Risen’: A Prophet’s Testimony” in the April 2012 Ensign. It is a magazine article, not a conference talk.
I declare my personal witness that death has been conquered, victory over the tomb has been won.
He built the road, and He walks it with us.
A rest stop with peace.
Alma learned that spirits go home to God. For the righteous, it is a place of rest. President Joseph F. Smith saw the faithful gathered together.

Now, concerning the state of the soul between death and the resurrection—Behold, it has been made known unto me by an angel, that the spirits of all men, as soon as they are departed from this mortal body, yea, the spirits of all men, whether they be good or evil, are taken home to that God who gave them life. And then shall it come to pass, that the spirits of those who are righteous are received into a state of happiness, which is called paradise, a state of rest, a state of peace, where they shall rest from all their troubles and from all care, and sorrow.

As I pondered over these things which are written, the eyes of my understanding were opened, and the Spirit of the Lord rested upon me, and I saw the hosts of the dead, both small and great. And there were gathered together in one place an innumerable company of the spirits of the just, who had been faithful in the testimony of Jesus while they lived in mortality;
President Thomas S. Monson of the First Presidency said this in his talk “I Know That My Redeemer Lives” from the April 2007 general conference.
Though difficult and painful, death is an essential part of our mortal experience.
It is a place to rest and wait.
Arrive whole.
At the end of the trip, the body and spirit are joined again. Every part is made whole. Nephi said this power is part of the Creator’s merciful plan.

The soul shall be restored to the body, and the body to the soul; yea, and every limb and joint shall be restored to its body; yea, even a hair of the head shall not be lost; but all things shall be restored to their proper and perfect frame.

For as death hath passed upon all men, to fulfil the merciful plan of the great Creator, there must needs be a power of resurrection, and the resurrection must needs come unto man by reason of the fall; and the fall came by reason of transgression; and because man became fallen they were cut off from the presence of the Lord.
Elder Dallin H. Oaks of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Resurrection” from the April 2000 general conference.
Because of the resurrection, we know that these mortal deficiencies are only temporary!
The weary traveler arrives rested and well.
The light is on.
Jesus told His friends that His Father’s house has many rooms, and that He would prepare a place for them. Peter wrote that the gospel is also taught to spirits who did not hear it in life.

In my Father’s house are many mansions: if it were not so, I would have told you. I go to prepare a place for you. And if I go and prepare a place for you, I will come again, and receive you unto myself; that where I am, there ye may be also.

For Christ also hath once suffered for sins, the just for the unjust, that he might bring us to God, being put to death in the flesh, but quickened by the Spirit: By which also he went and preached unto the spirits in prison;
President Thomas S. Monson of the First Presidency said this in his talk “I Know That My Redeemer Lives” from the April 2007 general conference.
Because our Savior died at Calvary, death has no hold upon any one of us.
Someone is waiting, and the light is on.
Comfort along the road.
We will cry along the way when someone we love is gone. The Lord says that is right. He also promises peace to those who die in Him, and a day with no more tears.

Thou shalt live together in love, insomuch that thou shalt weep for the loss of them that die, and more especially for those that have not hope of a glorious resurrection. And it shall come to pass that those that die in me shall not taste of death, for it shall be sweet unto them;
And God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes; and there shall be no more death, neither sorrow, nor crying, neither shall there be any more pain: for the former things are passed away.
Elder Dallin H. Oaks of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Resurrection” from the April 2000 general conference.
The assurance of immortality also helps us bear the mortal separations involved in the death of our loved ones.
We can grieve and still have hope.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time they felt hope while grieving. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Weep not

blocks.text: Jesus Christ met a funeral procession at the gate of a city. A widow was burying her only son.

Now when he came nigh to the gate of the city, behold, there was a dead man carried out, the only son of his mother, and she was a widow: and much people of the city was with her. And when the Lord saw her, he had compassion on her, and said unto her, Weep not. And he came and touched the bier: and they that bare him stood still. And he said, Young man, I say unto thee, Arise. And he that was dead sat up, and began to speak. And he delivered him to his mother.
The Savior saw her tears and felt compassion. He did not wait to be asked. He sees our tears too, and He promises a day when every family will be whole.

application.text: First, ask someone about a loved one they have lost. Second, listen without trying to fix anything. Third, say a short prayer for people who mourn.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know that the road does not end at death. I know that Jesus Christ made the way and prepared a place for us. I know that God sees every tear. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

invitations: I invite you to ask someone about a loved one they have lost.
I invite you to listen without trying to fix anything.
I invite you to say a short prayer for people who mourn.
blessings: Someone will feel safe to share.
Those who mourn will be comforted.

closingVerse.text: These things I have spoken unto you, that in me ye might have peace. In the world ye shall have tribulation: but be of good cheer; I have overcome the world.
